title: SK Group and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership Across AI Factories and Next-Generation Memory
summary: SK Group and NVIDIA today announced plans for a $500-billion-plus comprehensive partnership to establish AI infrastructure serving the surging demand for global compute. The two sides signed letters of intent to formalize the agreement, which spans from AI factory construction to AI memory supply.
body_text: News Summary: SK Group and NVIDIA expand strategic collaboration with a $500-billion-plus initiative spanning AI factories and next-generation memory. SK Telecom to build 2-gigawatt NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory to serve global compute demand. NVIDIA and SK hynix establish long-term partnership to secure and codevelop next-generation AI memory, including HBM. AI Summit — SK Group and NVIDIA today announced plans for a $500-billion-plus comprehensive partnership to establish AI infrastructure serving the surging demand for global compute. The two sides signed letters of intent to formalize the agreement, which spans from AI factory construction to AI memory supply. NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure and DSX Platform Drive 2-Gigawatt Build Today’s announcement builds on the decades-long technology partnership between SK Group and NVIDIA, including the recently announced plans for SK Telecom to build a 2-gigawatt-scale AI Cloud in Korea. This cloud will use the NVIDIA® DSX™ platform and deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin accelerated computing powered by SK hynix HBM4, with the first AI factory planned to come online in 2027. It will be built on the NVIDIA DSX full-stack AI factory architecture, which integrates NVIDIA accelerated computing, systems, software and partner technologies to deliver the lowest token cost at maximum energy efficiency. The two companies aim to accelerate large-scale AI infrastructure development, including sovereign, physical, agentic and enterprise AI services, and jointly address the increasing AI demand across the Asia-Pacific region, including South Korea. Accelerating AI Infrastructure at Scale The SK Telecom and NVIDIA collaboration accelerates the adoption of NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure and broadens customer access to advanced cloud services. The partnership enables SK Telecom to invest in and expand large-scale AI infrastructure while making capital-intensive AI infrastructure available to a broader range of customers. Advancing Next-Generation AI Memory SK hynix is also entering into a long-term AI memory partnership with NVIDIA. As a follow-up measure to solidify their previous long-term technical partnership, this agreement allows NVIDIA to secure a stable supply of next-generation AI memory, while enabling SK hynix to expand the foundation for growth. The two companies will codevelop and optimize next-generation AI memory solutions, including HBM, to meet evolving infrastructure demands ranging from large language model training to agentic AI and physical AI . “In the AI era, competitiveness depends not just on how effectively AI is utilized, but on how much intelligence we can produce,” said SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won. “By leveraging SK hynix’s AI memory and SK Telecom’s AI infrastructure capabilities, SK will collaborate with NVIDIA to build a world-class AI factory, helping Korea transcend its role as a leading adopter of AI and become a global hub that drives AI innovation.” “South Korea has all the ingredients to become a global AI powerhouse — world-class networks and data centers, leadership in chip technology and vast industrial scale,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Together with SK Telecom and SK hynix, we are building a new generation of AI factories that will power Korea’s next wave of growth.”

title: SafetyKit | The Take It Down Act (2025): What Platforms Need to Know About Federal NCII Compliance
summary: The Take It Down Act—effective May 2025—requires platforms to remove non-consensual intimate or AI-generated content within 48 hours. SafetyKit helps platforms stay compliant with AI-powered detection, automated takedowns, and audit-ready reporting.
body_text: On May 19, 2025, the Take It Down Act became the first federal law to directly regulate AI-generated content and impose mandatory takedown requirements on platforms. If you operate a website or app with user-generated content, you have until May 19, 2026 to implement compliant systems. Meeting these requirements requires sophisticated AI detection and automated workflows. SafetyKit provides AI-powered NCII detection systems that identify non-consensual intimate imagery and deepfakes at scale. Our customers use these systems to protect users and maintain compliance with federal requirements. What the Act Requires: Prohibitions and Platform Compliance The Take It Down Act creates federal liability for non-consensual distribution of intimate imagery and mandates platform action within 48 hours. Key prohibitions: Publishing intimate content or AI-generated deepfakes without consent (with intent to harm), any intimate imagery of minors, or threatening to share such content for coercion or extortion. Platform obligations: Accept victim reports with electronic signature and sufficient location information Remove content within 48 hours of valid notice Prevent re-uploads through duplicate detection Maintain audit trails of all takedown actions Failure to comply is treated as a violation of the FTC Act, with civil penalties reaching ~$51,000 per violation. Technical Requirements for Compliance Meeting the 48-hour deadline requires platforms to implement: AI-Powered Detection: Identify NCII and AI-generated deepfakes that evade traditional hash-matching Duplicate Prevention: Catch re-uploads even when content is cropped, filtered, or modified Automated Triage: Prioritize urgent reports within compliance windows FTC-Ready Audit Trails: Document every decision to demonstrate good faith efforts Cross-Account Monitoring: Track distribution patterns to prevent serial re-uploaders How SafetyKit Enables Compliance SafetyKit's AI platform detects, triages, and removes non-consensual intimate imagery in compliance with the Take It Down Act. Already deployed by leading marketplaces and UGC platforms, here's how we help: AI-Powered NCII Detection: Our models identify intimate imagery and deepfakes across images and video, including AI-generated content that evades traditional systems. 48-Hour Workflow Automation: From report intake to removal, SafetyKit automates compliance workflows while maintaining quality review standards. Cross-Account Re-Upload Prevention: Advanced perceptual hashing tracks content across accounts and catches duplicates, even when modified. FTC-Ready Audit Trails: Every detection and takedown is logged with timestamps and compliance metadata for safe harbor protection. Real-Time Monitoring: Dashboard visibility into report volumes, response times, and compliance rates enables proactive risk management. Take Action Now Enterprises deploying generative AI should view content abuse detection and mitigation as foundational system requirements, not optional features. Organizations that proactively address compliance will have competitive advantages: reduced regulatory risk, stronger user trust, and operational readiness for future regulations. SafetyKit can help your platform achieve compliance with the Take It Down Act. Our platform detects, triages, and removes non-consensual intimate imagery tailored to your product and risk profile. Contact us to discuss your compliance strategy and see how SafetyKit's AI-powered moderation platform can protect your users while meeting federal requirements. The Take It Down Act represents a turning point in content moderation and AI regulation. Platforms that take decisive action now will be better positioned to protect users, maintain compliance, and navigate the evolving regulatory landscape.

body_text: By Hardy Gaschler, Director of Operations When we began the transition of injection molding operations from Ludwigsstadt, Germany, to our site in Sonneberg, Germany, the objective was clear. The company needed to consolidate operations and improve efficiency. The reason for the move was straightforward. Continuing production in Ludwigsstadtis no longer practical. At the same time, Sonneberg has developed into experts in injection molding, making it the natural location for these operations. However, moving equipment is only one part of the story. The project required close coordination across multiple teams, including project leadership, manufacturing engineering, and planning. Weekly alignment meetings ensured that all stakeholders had a clear understanding of progress, risks, and priorities. One of the key challenges came from legacy constraints. In the past, tools were often dedicated to individual machines. This limited flexibility and made it more difficult to respond to increasing demand. As a result, the team needed to rethink how production capacity could be managed more effectively. The transition also highlighted the importance of investment in future capability. We are introducing new tools and considering additional machines. We are recreating clean room conditions in Sonneberg to meet production requirements. Although this project is primarily local, it reflects broader themes that are common in global organizations. Decisions about production and capacity are influenced by demand, supply chain considerations, and long-term strategy. This site move demonstrates how operational change and company culture are closely connected. The team is not only executing a transition. They are learning from past limitations and improving flexibility to prepare for future growth. The result will be more than a relocation. It will be a stronger and more resilient manufacturing operation. This is the Novanta Way in action.

title: Deutsche Bank expands escrow services in Korea, Vietnam and Malaysia
summary: Deutsche Bank expands escrow services in Korea, Vietnam and Malaysia
body_text: Deutsche Bank today announced the expansion of its escrow services in South Korea, Vietnam and Malaysia, strengthening its Trust and Securities Services offering in Asia Pacific and enabling clients to execute increasingly complex transactions with greater confidence. As cross-border activity accelerates and deal structures become more sophisticated, clients are placing greater emphasis on safeguarding assets throughout the lifecycle of a transaction. Escrow arrangements play a critical role by holding funds or assets with a neutral third party until predefined conditions are met, helping to mitigate counterparty, financial and regulatory risks. With this expansion, Deutsche Bank will provide on-the-ground escrow support in three high-growth markets that are attracting strong foreign investment and corporate activity. The move enhances the bank’s ability to support clients navigating mergers and acquisitions, project finance, capital raising and other transaction types where secure asset separation and conditional fund release are essential. Deutsche Bank’s escrow solutions combine global scale with local expertise. The bank supports escrow arrangements across multiple jurisdictions and currencies, offers standardised documentation to enable fast execution, and provides integrated access to foreign exchange, custody, cash management and reporting services. The service is designed to provide assurance to all parties in a transaction that funds are secured and will only be released when agreed milestones are achieved. This reduces settlement risk, supports smoother deal execution and builds trust between counterparties, particularly in cross-border or multi-party transactions. Expanding our escrow capabilities in South Korea, Vietnam and Malaysia reflects rising client demand for secure, transparent and efficient transaction structures across Asia Pacific. Our global platform, combined with deep local expertise, enables us to support clients confidently throughout the transaction lifecycle. Daniel Clark, Head of Trust and Securities Services for Asia Pacific and the Middle East & Africa The addition of South Korea, Vietnam and Malaysia builds on Deutsche Bank’s established escrow capabilities across Asia Pacific and globally, where it supports clients with dedicated specialists, efficient know-your-client processes and a wide range of investment options for escrow balances. By expanding into these markets, Deutsche Bank is further reinforcing its position as a trusted partner for secure escrow solutions, supporting clients as they pursue growth opportunities across the region.
